result.title: OpenStripe supports open-set identification and spatial stripe profiling in wild Amur tigers
result.comment: 14 pages, 4 figures. Code and nonspatial data: https://github.com/Yichun-Peng/OpenStripe
result.summary: Non-invasive camera-trap monitoring of endangered wildlife requires open-set individual identification---grouping field images into identities without predefined classes or a known population size---yet pose deformation and cluttered backgrounds complicate image comparison. Here, we present OpenStripe, a multi-agent framework that reconstructs canonical two-dimensional (2D) tiger torso patterns and encodes four interpretable local stripe structures: breakpoints, bifurcations, irregular structures, and round structures. We evaluated OpenStripe on 100 camera-trap records from 28 wild Amur tigers (Panthera tigris altaica), representing nearly one-third of the documented population in the Northeast China Tiger and Leopard National Park. Combining all four complementary structures enabled automatic identity grouping with 0.90 matched accuracy and a 0.85 adjusted Rand index (ARI), outperforming 49 baseline configurations under the same backend (up to 0.43 accuracy and 0.14 ARI). In addition, results from OpenStripe indicate that stripe similarity in Amur tigers declines with geographic distance and suggest that traits such as fractal dimension and inter-stripe spacing are associated with geographic proximity. OpenStripe thus provides an interpretable representation that connects automated individual grouping with spatial phenotypic profiling in wild populations.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 OpenStripe，一个用于野生东北虎红外相机图像的多智能体框架，重建虎躯干二维规范图案并编码四类可解释条纹局部结构，实现开放集个体识别，并分析条纹相似度与地理距离的关系。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于野生动物个体识别与空间表型分析的应用工作，虽涉及多智能体和可解释局部特征，但不涉及 VLM 推理状态、证据获取、停止决策或 latent 内容的使用，与 LVR 主线缺少实质联系。
